concept.name: Volume oscillator
concept.definition: A MACD-style oscillator applied to volume: the difference between a fast and a slow exponential moving average of volume, usually expressed as a percentage of the slow average (the Percentage Volume Oscillator, defaults 12, 26, 9).
concept.intuition: It shows whether participation is expanding or drying up: positive and rising means short-term volume is running above its longer norm.
concept.mechanics: PVO = (EMA(V,12) - EMA(V,26)) / EMA(V,26) x 100, with a 9-period EMA signal line and a histogram, paralleling the MACD/PPO structure. Used mainly to confirm breakouts - price breaks on rising or positive PVO carry more weight.
concept.formula: PVO = ((EMA(V,12) - EMA(V,26)) / EMA(V,26)) x 100; Signal = EMA(PVO, 9); Histogram = PVO - Signal.
concept.failure_modes: Volume does not trend smoothly, so PVO is choppy and divergences are unreliable; because both EMAs lag, PVO can confirm a breakout only after the fact.
concept.misconceptions: A positive PVO does not say volume is 'high' in any absolute sense - only that the 12-period average exceeds the 26-period; and high volume is neither bullish nor bearish without price context.
concept.example: A 12-day volume EMA of 3.0M against a 26-day EMA of 2.5M gives PVO = +20, matching the surge level StockCharts shows confirming ADM's resistance and support breaks.
